question: Which measured component causes the T251 steady-state and tail latency failures: exact T247 graph inference, Python host work, cyclic garbage collection, or residual CPU-7 kernel work?

arms_in_fixed_order.instrumentation: exact locomotion ONNX session stage/commit timing only
method-boundary timing for observation, ONNX, target pipeline, observer, residual host, and commit

measurement.hot_loop_storage: preallocated numpy arrays; all JSON/NPZ serialization after each arm
measurement.raw_output: one compressed NPZ outside the repository plus its SHA-256 receipt
measurement.compact_output: one reviewed JSON result with summaries and the 64 worst ticks per arm
system_snapshots: process voluntary and involuntary context switches
semantic_canaries: full-host GC enabled and disabled action traces are byte-identical
exact 250/0/10000 state chain in both full-host arms
no robot device descriptor before or after

classification_rule.steady_graph_floor: If graph-only p99 exceeds 2.0 ms, the unchanged exact ONNX graph is itself above the T251 steady limit; Python-only host optimization cannot earn a rerun.
classification_rule.steady_host_overhead: If graph-only p99 is at most 2.0 ms but GC-disabled full-host p99 exceeds 2.0 ms, optimize only the measured host components before a corrected run.
classification_rule.gc_tail: If disabling GC removes the over-5-ms tail from the full host while graph-only also remains at most 5.0 ms, register hot-loop GC suppression plus off-loop collection.
classification_rule.kernel_or_graph_tail: If graph-only retains over-5-ms events with GC disabled, use context-switch/interrupt deltas and worst-tick spacing to distinguish residual kernel work from graph execution; do not guess.
classification_rule.mixed: If more than one mechanism remains, correct every evidenced contributor before any new gate run.

decision_rule.diagnostic_complete: File the compact result and raw receipt, then preregister exactly one evidence-selected implementation correction.
